Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can size the POC and the security review: 

Summary of what I heard you say: 
- You need request/response logs for debugging customer issues for 30 days.
- You want headers sanitized so that any internal trace identifiers are not stored in plaintext in logs (CareSync prefers masked/hashed trace IDs).
- Data residency requirement: EU only for production, but POC may live in a US region if we agree on encryption and access controls.

Questions / assumptions: 
1) When you say "request/response logs" — do you need full request/response bodies for 30 days, or would a sampled set (e.g., 1%) + structured metadata suffice for debugging?
2) For trace IDs and cookies: are you OK with truncated+hashed identifiers (we can provide deterministic hashing so you can correlate across systems without raw values), or do you require complete removal?
3) Will your security team require a SOC 2 artifact review for the POC? If so, what timeline do they expect?

Next steps we propose: 
- Ben to scope redaction options and performance impact (we expect negligible token-cost change for server-side masking).
- Marcus to put together a mini-MAP (mutual action plan) and timeline for a 2-week POC including acceptance criteria.
- Schedule a short technical session with your engineering and security leads (30–45min).

I've attached a short checklist of redaction patterns we've used previously and a one-pager on our hashing approach for trace IDs.

Would a tech call on Tuesday 10/13 at 10am PT work for you?

Thanks,

Olga —

Thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline: 

> 1) Full bodies vs sampled set
We need full request/response bodies for the following endpoints for 30 days: /api/v1/triage, /api/v1/notes, and webhook events. For other endpoints, sampling at 5% is fine. The reason: clinical debugging on triage flows needs the payload to reproduce issues.

> 2) Trace IDs and cookies
We cannot have raw trace IDs or cookies in stored logs. Deterministic hashing is acceptable provided the hash uses a salt we agree on and you can demonstrate that hashes are one-way. We also prefer header minimization at ingress (strip X-Internal-Auth, remove any cookie values) and retention of only a safe allowlist of headers (User-Agent, Content-Type, X-Request-ID-hash).

> 3) SOC 2 artifacts
Yes. Our security team will request SOC 2 Type II evidence for any contract > $50k ARR. For the POC I expect a lighter review — a security questionnaire + shared SOC 2 summary will do.

On POC region: we can accept US for the POC provided all logs are encrypted at rest with customer BYOK and access is restricted to named Redwood operators. Production will be EU-only.

We can do Tue 10/13 10am PT — I booked it and included our lead infra engineer (cc'd on eng@).

Elena Morales
Director of Integrations | CareSync
elena.morales@caresync.com

Hi team / Elena —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Quick technical readout and options we can offer for the POC and later production: 

What Redwood can do (options):
- Ingress redaction layer: run a lightweight filter at the API edge that strips disallowed headers and applies deterministic HMAC_SHA256(salt) to trace IDs and cookies. This happens before logs are emitted so no raw values hit our log storage.
- Field-level redaction rules: configurable allowlist/blocklist per endpoint. For the three sensitive endpoints Elena noted we can set body-retention rules to keep full payloads for 30 days in encrypted log storage; other endpoints default to 5% sample rate.
- Access controls & BYOK: POC with US region + customer-managed keys (KMS) is possible; we can document operator access and provide audit logs. Production will be pinned to eu-west-1 with the same redaction rules.
- Hashing guarantees: we use salt-per-customer and HMAC to ensure deterministic but non-reversible IDs. We can provide a short whitepaper and a reproducible test vector for your security review.

Estimated impact: ingress redaction adds ~3–8ms p95 to request path (depends on payload size). Sampling & retention are orthogonal and mostly affect storage costs, not latency.

Proposed POC acceptance criteria (to include in the MAP):
1) Demonstrate that ingested logs for /api/v1/triage retain full payloads with controlled access and are available for investigation within 5 minutes.
2) Show that trace IDs present in logs are hashed with customer salt and cannot be reversed.
3) Confirm region + BYOK configuration for POC and outline operator access list.
4) Security questionnaire completed and SOC 2 summary shared within two weeks.

Deliverables & timeline (2-week POC):
- Day 0–2: Environment setup (US region) + BYOK key exchange.
- Day 3–6: Apply ingress redaction rules and retention policy; run 1st ingest tests.
- Day 7–10: End-to-end debugging scenario with CareSync team (confirm acceptance criteria 1–2).
- Day 11–14: Provide SOC 2 artifacts and finalize MAP for production (EU cutover plan).

Attachments: care_sync_mini_map.xlsx (timeline + owners), redaction-patterns.pdf (examples).
